cards.design_implication: Consider integrating terrestrial experimental data (e.g., from heavy-ion collisions) with astrophysical observations to refine theoretical models of high-density matter.
does_not_establish: The specific mathematical formulation of the Bayesian inference.
Generalizability to heavy-ion collisions of nuclei other than gold.
The precise magnitude of the pressure increase without further data analysis.
cards.evidence_excerpt: Here we use Bayesian inference to combine data from astrophysical multi-messenger observations of neutron stars 1–9 and from heavy-ion collisions of gold nuclei at relativistic energies 10,11 with microscopic nuclear theory calculations 12–17 to improve our understanding of dense matter.
limitations: Scope limited to the specific combination of neutron star observations, gold nucleus collisions, and microscopic nuclear theory described.
Abstract level; does not specify the exact statistical methods or priors used in the Bayesian inference.
cards.statement: Incorporating data from heavy-ion collision experiments into joint analyses with astrophysical observations improves constraints on dense matter, specifically indicating an increase in pressure.
